fixes.explanation: Right on the money, baker. Haggai 2:20 says it's "For the second time that day…" on the twenty-fourth day of the month. Haggai, a prophet (Haggai 2:1), gets two words from the LORD in one day. I'd be tired just carrying the mail.

Close, but the text doesn't make him wait. Haggai 2:20 says "For the second time that day…" so no days pass at all. Haggai, a prophet (Haggai 2:1), gets both words on the twenty-fourth. Nobody has to check the mailbox for three days.

A whole month would be a long wait, friend. But Haggai 2:20 says "For the second time that day, the twenty-fourth day of the month…" Haggai, a prophet (Haggai 2:1), hears from the LORD twice in one day. No calendar flipping needed.
Prophet is a fair guess, since Haggai is right there. But Haggai is the prophet in this scene (Haggai 2:1). The LORD tells Zerubbabel, "…I will take you, My servant…" (Haggai 2:23)
A staff is a nice picture, but it's not the one here. The LORD says, "…I will make you like My signet ring…" (Haggai 2:23) Zerubbabel is made like a ring, friend, not like a staff.
